S57.01.needs: a signed-in account where web search is available on the plan; the tester should confirm the plan first
S57.01.note: Tests say automatic web search is not a user-facing menu toggle, so the attach-menu entry may only apply to a local scope; the tester should check which control appears on the account.
steps: Sign in and open a new chat.
Open the attach menu in the composer and choose Search the web (or turn on Web search if the composer shows it).
Type a question that needs current facts, such as today's news, and send.
Look for a row or card that starts with 'Web search:' followed by the query and a result count, with sources listed under the answer. Compare with Expected: the search and its sources are shown.
S57.01.where: New chat > composer attach menu > Search the web, or the composer's Web search option; ask a question that needs current facts

S57.31.needs: an account that can run a tool in chat (a web search is enough)
S57.31.note: The "Request" block depends on the showParameters prop (default true); I did not confirm the chat page leaves it on.
steps: Start a chat and send a message that makes the assistant use a tool, for example a web search.
When the reply shows the tool row, click the row that reads "Tool run complete" to open the list.
Click one tool call row to open it.
Look for the "Request" heading; the block under it should show the command, file, query or JSON the tool was called with, and compare it with Expected.
S57.31.where: Chat reply > the row "Tool run complete" (click to open) > click a tool call row > "Request" block

S57.32.needs: an account that can run a tool in chat (a web search is enough)
S57.32.note: The per-tool running phrase comes from each tool's statusPhrase, and the "completed" wording comes from runStatusLabel in @agiworkforce/types, so exact wording varies by tool; the elapsed time is a formatted duration, not a fixed word.
steps: Send a message that makes the assistant run a tool, for example a web search or a file read.
While the reply is still coming, look at the tool row; it should show a running phrase such as "Working..." in blue, and the tool card shows a live elapsed time.
Wait for the run to finish.
Look at the row again: it should read "Tool run complete" with no running phrase, and a finished tool card shows its duration; compare with Expected.
S57.32.where: Chat: send a message that makes the assistant use a tool, then watch the tool row above the reply while it runs

S57.33.needs: an account that can run a tool in chat (a web search is enough)
S57.33.note: The code shows the full result in a box with a maximum height and a scrollbar, not a cut-down summary; I did not confirm a cut-off.
steps: Send a message that makes the assistant use a tool that returns a result, for example a web search.
When the run finishes, click the row that reads "Tool run complete".
Click a finished tool call row.
Look at the "Response" block; it should show a short preview of the result in a box that scrolls, and compare with Expected.
S57.33.where: Chat reply > the row "Tool run complete" (click to open) > click a finished tool call row > "Response" block

Open a connector that is already connected and has been used in a chat.
Click "Tool permissions" in its details.
Scroll to "Recent calls" and look at each entry's status ("Worked", "Failed" or "Blocked here") and its time; compare with Expected.
